chapter: Earl Hines, Chicago and later gigs
title: Jamming with Roy Eldridge and Ammons versus working with them
summary: He jammed but never worked with them in Chicago, and distinguishes a one-night pickup from working with a leader.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: Well, didn't you say you also worked with Roy in Chicago?
I didn't work with him. I jammed with him in Chicago.
No, I didn't work with Roy then. But Scoop Carey and them were working. But I'd go down and jam with him. No, I never did really work with Roy in Chicago

because this was after Roy was with Fletcher in Chicago that he got this little group of his own going over there. He and Chu were with Fletcher out in Chicago, Chu Berry. I didn't work with him. No, I just jammed with him out there. Like I didn't work with Albert Ammons but I jammed with him.

And maybe some nights if a guy and a gig for that night, he said, look, come on play with me and I'll give you X amount of dollars or something. I'd play that night but I wouldn't consider that working with a guy, you know. That would be just maybe a one-nighter with the guy or something. I've played with so many I couldn't even recall all the bands that I've played with like that. Just get paid for a night or a couple nights or something like that.
